chunks: And Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Muhammad al-Khayyat, from Mujammi', who said:
I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: “I take garments on contract to sew them, then I give them to the young workers for two-thirds.”
He said: “Do you not also work on them?”
I said: “I cut them and buy the threads for them.”
He said: “There is no harm in that.”

key_terms.أَتَقَبَّلُ: I take on work by contract
key_terms.الثِّيَابَ: garments or clothes to be sewn
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to subcontract work and keep a share of the payment?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the permissibility of subcontracting sewing work while taking a share of the payment. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام permits it when the person also contributes labor and supplies materials, indicating a lawful basis for shared compensation in work arrangements.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3912 - Safwan bin Yahya narrated from Abu Muhammad Al-Khayyat, from Mujammi', who said: 
I said to Abu Abdillah (as),
"I take on garments to sew and then give them to young workers, keeping one-third and giving them two-thirds. Is this permissible?"
Imam (as) said: "Don't you also work on them?"
I said: "I cut the fabric and buy the threads for them."
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in that."
